---
title: "Models"
---

`lm()`, `glm()`, `lmer()`, and `glmer()` pass the table to the phit extension's
`Phit\fit_lm()`, `Phit\fit_glm()`, `Phit\fit_lmer()`, and `Phit\fit_glmer()`.
phplyr adds no model code of its own. phit reads factor levels from the table,
builds the model matrix from an R formula, and fits the model.

::: {.panel-tabset group="syntax"}

## PHP 8.5+

```php
$table |> lm('y ~ x + group');
$table |> glm('passed ~ hours', family: 'binomial');
$table |> lmer('score ~ hours + (1 | school)');
$table |> glmer('passed ~ hours + (1 | school)', family: 'binomial');
```

## PHP 8.3–8.4

```php
phplyr($table)->lm('y ~ x + group');
phplyr($table)->glm('passed ~ hours', family: 'binomial');
phplyr($table)->lmer('score ~ hours + (1 | school)');
phplyr($table)->glmer('passed ~ hours + (1 | school)', family: 'binomial');
```

:::

| Function | Model | Options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lm($formula)` | Linear regression | |
| `glm($formula, family:)` | Generalized linear model | `family: 'gaussian'` (the default), `'binomial'`, or `'poisson'`, and `link:` |
| `lmer($formula)` | Linear mixed model with lme4's random-effect terms, such as `(1 \| school)` | REML by default; `reml: false` fits by maximum likelihood |
| `glmer($formula, family:)` | Generalized linear mixed model | `family: 'binomial'` by default |

Other named arguments go to phit's function unchanged. phit's documentation
lists them and the formula syntax it accepts.

## Results

Each function returns phit's result array in place of a table, so it ends a
method chain. `columns` holds R's coefficient names, in R's order, and
`coefficients`, `std_errors`, `p_values`, and `conf_int` follow the same order.
The array also has the fitted values, residuals, fit statistics such as
`r_squared` and `sigma`, and `n_observations` and `n_dropped`, which count the
rows used and the rows dropped for missing values.

{{< include ../examples/_models.md >}}

## Without the extension

Without phit, the four functions throw a `RuntimeException` that names the
missing phit function.

[phit-polyfill](https://github.com/phpstats/phit-polyfill) defines the same
functions in PHP for systems without the extension, and phplyr calls them the
same way. phplyr's test suite checks `lm()` and `glm()` against R with the
extension. With phit-polyfill and without the extension, the same `lm()` and
`glm()` cases gave R's coefficients within 1e-12 relative, checked by hand on
2026-10-31. phplyr's tests do not run the polyfill.
